# Open Questions

Format: `Q-xxx` · owner · blocking? · context · options/recommendation. When resolved, move to "Resolved" with the answer + linked decision.

## Open

### Q-005 — How are the "Source A–D" feedback channels interpreted?
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context: Sources are anonymized. Observed patterns (`documents/data-inventory.md` §1) are hypotheses only:
  - **A:** multi-country (incl. JP/KR), lower-case normalized, possibly translated.
  - **B:** US only, third-person "Customer stated…" notes.
  - **C:** US only, structured survey prompts ("I had a minor/serious problem…", "What is…"), mostly Difficult-to-Use/Defect.
  - **D:** US only; short; unclassified. Two prompt templates in G60 (checked 2026-10-10): 34 of 136 end with "That is the one thing could be most improved about the <area> of my vehicle" (improvement answers, e.g. "the head rests are too short"); the rest are mostly "love the…" answers. So D mixes "what do you like" and "what could be most improved" — the earlier note that D is **not** improvement feedback was wrong.
- This affects source-trust weighting. Don't weight sources differently until confirmed.

### Q-006 — Customer study scales
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context:
  - The CN_EU sheet has numeric means in the range ~6.5–9.9 (0–10 or 1–10?).
  - The US sheet is a 7-point distribution ("I Hate It" … "I Love It").
  - **Neither sheet has sample sizes** — ask for n per model/market.
- Needed to compare/normalize, and to judge whether differences are meaningful.

### Q-007 — Team roles & who is the "PM" in the demo?
- Owner: team

### Q-008 — Hackathon logistics
- Owner: team
- Questions: submission deadline, demo length, required format (video/live/slides), judging criteria.

### Q-011 — How detailed can plant/platform reference data be?
- Owner: team
- Context: public sources give plant ↔ model/platform mapping and NK timing, rarely capacity or flexibility. Decide what granularity we claim, and mark the rest as assumptions.

### Q-013 — Market profile sources
- Owner: team
- Context: D-011 needs climate/usage/culture per market. Use research agents + cited sources (mobility studies, climate data, J.D. Power China/US).
- How deep do we go? EU as one market or split (DE vs. GB vs. Nordics)? Note that F70 feedback is 32% Japan and G60/G70 have KR/JP feedback (RoW).
- Recommendation: EU / US / CN (+ RoW where data exists) for the demo; the data model already supports countries.

### Q-015 — Are the BMW sales volumes real or illustrative?
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context: `sales_volumes.xlsx` conflicts with public data:
  - Its values are round thousands (all but one).
  - G60/G68 China is 68k → 75k (+10%) for 2024 → 2025, while public figures say 5 Series China (China-built, CPCA) Jan–Nov 2025 = 107,348 and BMW+MINI China fell 12.5%.
  - F70 EU 85k vs. 1 Series Europe 91,931 (Dataforce).
  - There is no powertrain split, although the briefing promised one.
- Also: F70 China 2024 is a formula cell (`=-D3-C10`, value 0) — another sign the file was constructed (2026-10-10).
- Until answered: use the file as BMW-internal relative weights, don't blend it with public figures, and show the conflict (`data-inventory.md` §3, `portfolio-reference.md` §4).

### Q-016 — Is driver assistance (ADAS) in scope?
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context:
  - BMW's process image (image_2) lists *Driver assistance* and *Powertrain* as requirement groups.
  - ADAS is a top purchase driver in China (`competitor-landscape.md` §2).
  - But "safety" is out of scope (regulatory).
- Working line (not decided): ADAS *experience* (usability, availability, comfort, trust) is in; safety/homologation performance is out.

### Q-024 — Leftovers from Q-021/Q-023 (evidence changes on decided requirements, web contradictions)
- Owner: team · not blocking
- Context: D-038 closed most of Q-021 and Q-023. Two parts are still open:
  - **Q-021 (b):** the linker still adds links to approved/deferred requirements directly in each wave. Rules 5/6 and the brief count evidence changes as decision-relevant, so they could become `link_finding` change proposals for the PM instead.
  - **Q-023, contradictions:** web findings with `contradicts=true` still don't affect the score; only `supports` count. Study items already work both ways through the z-score.
- Options: (a) leave both as they are and show them in the text only; (b) proposals for decided requirements plus a confidence cut when contradicting web evidence exists. Recommendation: (b), if there's time before the demo.

Your mission

Build an AI-powered application that ingests heterogeneous data, derives customer requirements for a vehicle, prioritizes them, and puts a product manager in the loop at the decisions that matter.

Your app should be able to:
•    Ingest the provided data and enrich it with structured knowledge from the web.
•    Extract signals such as recurring complaints, unmet needs, competitor advantages and market trends, each linked to its sources.
•    Derive requirements from those findings: clear, actionable, customer-facing and realistic.
•    Prioritize them with a logic you define and can explain.
•    Involve the PM to approve, reject, edit or challenge requirements and their rationale and evidence behind them.
•    Record everything in an audit trail (is a complete, chronological record of all actions, changes, and access events within a system or data environment).


About the Scope

In scope:
•    Customer requirements on the product: features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services, design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as experienced by the customer, variant and package offering, etc.

Out of scope:
•    Regulatory and homologation requirements (e.g.: safety, emissions, type approval)
•    Technical and engineering requirements (e.g.: component specs, architecture, supplier topics)
•    Pricing, business case and cost calculation (you may use cost or effort as a rough prioritization factor)


Make it yours!

Demonstrate your application at least for one derivative in onbe market but avoid designing it as a one-off: it should be adaptable to other BMW vehicles and markets. The remaining datasets and scenarios are available for optional testing.
We know the challenge is broad. Focus on the parts where your team can make the strongest contribution. You might go deep on web research and turn external information into usable evidence, or on integrating and interpreting the provided BMW data. You do not need to develop every capability to the same depth. Be creative, but show how your chosen focus connects to the overall path from evidence to a PM decision.
![data_and_source.png](data_and_source.png)


Expected Deliverables

A concept and demonstrable prototype of an AI-powered product requirements application that processes heterogeneous inputs, derives product requirements, supports prioritization, and integrates human review.

A structured sample list of derived product requirements. Each requirement should include a unique identifier, a clear and actionable description, its linked findings and sources, a priority or score, the applied prioritization rationale, an evidence level, the key future-facing assumptions and uncertainties and its current decision status.

A clearly defined end-to-end workflow showing how inputs are processed into proposed and prioritized requirements, which activities the AI performs autonomously, and where human review is mandatory.

A demonstrable audit trail that makes each requirement traceable from its underlying findings and sources through consolidation, scoring, prioritization, and human decision-making. It should record relevant changes to requirement content, scores, priorities, evidence, and status, including who or what initiated each change, when it occurred, and the documented rationale.

Important: Teams are free to choose their technical approach, architecture, prioritization logic, and user experience. The deliverables describe the capabilities and outcomes that should be demonstrated, not a prescribed solution design. Deliverables may be presented as one integrated solution or as a combination of connected concepts, prototypes, models, and visualizations.
# Challenge Brief — BMW "AI for Product Decision Making"

Source: `challange information document/BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf`, `mission.md`, `image_1.png`, `image_2.png`, `data_and_source.png`.

## The question

> What should the next generation of a BMW vehicle offer its customers?

Build an AI-powered app that helps **product managers (PMs)** derive, justify and prioritize **customer requirements** for a **successor vehicle**, grounded in customer feedback, BMW product + sales data, and web research — with the **PM firmly in control of every decision**.

Why (PDF): turning large volumes of feedback, market signals, competitor info and product data into requirements is today "largely manual, time-consuming, and difficult to trace consistently".

- Vehicles: BMW **1 Series (F70)**, **5 Series (G60, China LWB = G68)**, **7 Series (G70)** — any one or a combination. (The PDF says only "1/5/7 Series"; the e-codes come from the data files.)
- Markets: **Europe, China, US** — any subset.
- **Minimum:** demonstrate at least **one derivative in one market**, but don't design a one-off; it must be adaptable to other vehicles/markets. The remaining datasets/scenarios are *optional* testing material (mission.md).
- Horizon: **3–5 years ahead** (needs at successor launch, not just today).
- Definition: **Customer Requirement = Customer-relevant attribute of a car.**
- Must make clear **what is evidence vs. forward-looking assumption**.

## The app must be able to

1. **Ingest** provided data and **enrich** with structured web knowledge.
2. **Extract signals** — recurring complaints, unmet needs, competitor advantages, market trends — **each linked to sources**.
3. **Derive requirements** — clear, actionable, customer-facing, realistic.
4. **Prioritize** — with a logic we define and can explain.
5. **Involve the PM** — approve, reject, edit, or challenge requirements, rationale and evidence.
6. **Audit trail** — complete chronological record of all actions, changes, access events.

## Scope

**In:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment & digital services, design & quality perception, driving experience, range & charging *as experienced by the customer*, variant & package offering.

**Out:** regulatory/homologation (safety, emissions, type approval); technical/engineering (component specs, architecture, suppliers); pricing / business case / cost calculation (rough cost/effort as a prioritization factor is OK).

### Scope tensions (unresolved — don't paper over them)

- **Platform/plant feasibility vs. "architecture" out of scope.** BMW's out-of-scope list names "architecture". Vehicle platforms (CLAR, FAAR, NK) arguably *are* that. D-009 uses platform/plant data as a feasibility gate, which is our addition and not asked for by BMW. It also rests mostly on trade-press reference data. Open with BMW mentors: Q-010.
- **Driver assistance vs. "safety" out of scope.** BMW's own process image lists *Driver assistance* (and *Powertrain*) as requirement groups, and ADAS-as-experienced is a top purchase driver in China. But safety requirements are out of scope. Our working line: ADAS *experience* (usability, availability, comfort) is in; safety/homologation performance is out. Open: Q-016.
- **"Business" prioritization dimension vs. no business case.** image_2 shows *Customer* and *Business* dimensions. We use market volume and rough effort only — no pricing or business-case math.

## Expected deliverables (checklist)

- [ ] **Concept + demonstrable prototype** — heterogeneous inputs → derived requirements → prioritization → human review.
- [ ] **Structured sample requirement list**. Each requirement has:
  - [ ] unique ID
  - [ ] clear, actionable description
  - [ ] linked findings and sources
  - [ ] priority / score
  - [ ] applied prioritization rationale
  - [ ] evidence level
  - [ ] key future-facing assumptions & uncertainties
  - [ ] current decision status
- [ ] **End-to-end workflow definition** — what AI does autonomously, where human review is mandatory.
- [ ] **Demonstrable audit trail** — requirement traceable from sources → findings → consolidation → scoring → prioritization → human decision; records changes to content, scores, priorities, evidence, status, with **who/what**, **when**, **rationale**.

The PDF ("What to demonstrate") phrases the same as three items:
1. **Concept and working prototype**: AI supports identification, formulation and prioritization of customer-facing requirements from the provided data and, where relevant, external sources.
2. **Representative set of requirements with clear evidence and reasoning**: show how feedback, product data, market signals or competitor insights become requirements, and explain what drives their priority.
3. **Transparent decision-support experience**: PMs can **review, challenge, modify, approve or reject** AI proposals. Evidence, assumptions, uncertainties and key decisions stay visible and traceable.

Freedom of approach:
- Teams choose the technical approach, architecture, prioritization logic and UX.
- Deliverables may be one integrated solution or connected concepts, prototypes, models and visualizations (mission.md).
- BMW is interested in how the solution turns information into insight and makes reasoning transparent, "**not in a specific workflow or technical architecture**" (PDF). → Don't over-invest in architecture at the expense of the demo.

## BMW's reference process (image_2.png)

1. **Situation analysis** — baseline (previous BMW model, BMW portfolio, sales volume; AI + human) + competition, customer/public feedback, product & global trends (AI).
2. **Structure & context** — classify, cluster, contextualize: AI standardizes findings, identifies duplicates, groups themes, connects insights → list of all potential requirements (0/1: implement?), e.g. BEV powertrain, cooler, seat ventilation. (AI)
3. **Requirements definition** — specification & quantification: measurable targets + acceptance criteria (e.g. "Range: 600 or 700 mi?", "Cooler for how many bottles?", "Seat ventilation: fast enough?"), grouped by Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver assistance / … (AI + human)
4. **Prioritization** — Customer, Business, … dimensions. (AI + human)
5. **Documentation** — requirements tracking (shown as a cycle). (AI)

## Provided data, promised vs. delivered (`data_and_source.png`)

| Dataset | BMW says | Reality (see `data-inventory.md`) |
|---|---|---|
| Customer verbatims | free text on the current vehicle → pain points, unmet needs, must-not-lose | ✓; no China verbatims, no dates |
| Equipment list | standard/optional equipment "by trim and market" | German price lists only |
| Sales volumes | units "by powertrain and region" | region only, no powertrain; values look stylized (Q-015) |
| Customer study | ratings in various categories | ✓; CN/EU means vs. US 7-point distributions, no sample sizes |

## Judging signals (what BMW says it values)

- Trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning.
- Thoughtful prioritization.
- Clear handling of **uncertainty and conflicting evidence**.
- Customer value over engineering specs / regulation / business case.
- **Scalability** across vehicle lines, markets, future decisions → **don't build a one-off**.
- Focus is free: go deep where we're strongest, but show how it connects to the full path evidence → PM decision.

## BMW mentor clarifications (Discord, 2026-10-10)

Common PM pain points from BMW. **This is a paraphrase** — TODO: paste the verbatim Discord message (author, timestamp) here so the source is traceable.

1. **Balancing customer requirements across markets/regions.** Preferences differ by **climate, real-world usage and culture** — what works in one market can fail in another. → Never treat "the customer" as one group (D-011).
2. **Getting early customer feedback and extracting *future* requirements**, e.g. from feedback on predecessor vehicles. → Project what customers will want at successor launch, not just what they complained about (D-012).
3. **The requirements process is ongoing (~2 years), not a one-time list.** The most relevant requirements are re-prioritized again and again. → Continuous re-prioritization with history, so the PM sees how and why priorities changed (D-013).
4. *(BMW support, 2026-10-10)* **Use the BMW Group Report 2025** to ground ideas: (a) market & sales data (regional growth, deliveries by model series, EV adoption) for personas, demand and impact; (b) product strategy & R&D (R&D priorities, ConnectedDrive/My BMW App, NEUE KLASSE) to show alignment with BMW's investments and future architecture. → Extract in `bmw-annual-report-2025.md`. Note: alignment with BMW strategy is context for prioritization, not engineering output (scope).
# Architecture & Workflow

> **As built (2026-10-10):** the workflow below is implemented end to end — modules per step in the repo `README.md`; decisions D-024–D-033. Deviations from this concept: findings span all markets of a derivative with per-market/per-wave metrics (not one finding per market); feasibility is non-blocking (D-030); market fit is a score modifier; requirement status is per requirement, priority per target.

**Status: DRAFT v3 — conceptual.** The workflow, entities and rules below are the agreed *concept* (D-005, D-008–D-013). The *technical* stack is decided (LangGraph, SQLite, sqlite-vec, no graph DB, Streamlit — D-015–D-020, see `tech-stack.md`). The data model below is built in SQLite (`src/bmw_req/db.py`) per D-021, with three entities folded in: `segment` → `vehicle_model.segment`, `market_profile` → columns on `market`, `finding_scope` → scope columns on `finding`. Added: `source_item.country`, `source_embedding` (sqlite-vec), `llm_cache`.

## Guiding principle

BMW decides at **portfolio level** — across shared platforms (CLAR, FAAR, Neue Klasse), plants and markets — not one car at a time. The data model is therefore **multi-brand, multi-derivative, multi-market, platform- and plant-aware from day one**. The 5 Series (G60 + China LWB G68) is the deepest worked example; F70 and G70 run through the same pipeline.

## End-to-end workflow

| # | Stage | Actor | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Ingest** BMW data (feedback, study, sales, option lists) for all derivatives × markets | AI (autonomous) | `source_item` with provenance (file, sheet, row) and scope (derivative, market) |
| 2 | **Load reference data** — platforms, plants, brand positioning, segments, competitor models | AI-researched, **human-curated** | reference tables, each fact with source + date (`portfolio-reference.md`, `competitor-landscape.md` are the seeds) |
| 3 | **Enrich via web research agents** — competitors, sales, demand, reviews, trends, customer expectations (see `knowledge-base.md`) | AI (autonomous), PM can accept/reject sources | `source_item(kind=web)` with URL, date, publisher, trust tier, quote |
| 4 | **Extract signals** — classify, dedupe, cluster into findings: complaint / unmet need / must-not-lose delighter / competitor advantage / market trend / brand expectation | AI (autonomous) | `finding` with scope (derivative / platform / market / portfolio), linked sources, metrics |
| 5 | **Derive requirements** — customer-facing, actionable, measurable target + acceptance criteria; scoped to one or more derivatives × markets | AI proposes | `requirement` (status `proposed`) + `requirement_target` rows |
| 6 | **Fit & feasibility checks** per target (D-008, D-009): brand fit, segment fit, market fit, platform/plant feasibility | AI checks, flags explained | `fit_check` rows: pass / warn / fail + rationale + evidence |
| 7 | **Score & prioritize** — explainable factors incl. market volume and portfolio leverage (`requirement-model.md`) | AI computes, PM adjusts weights | score breakdown + rationale |
| 8 | **PM review** — approve / reject / edit / challenge / defer; override failed checks only with rationale | **Human (mandatory)** | status change + rationale |
| 9 | **Document & export** — requirement list, portfolio view, full audit trail | AI | JSON / XLSX export, audit timeline per requirement |

### It's a loop, not a one-shot (D-013)

The requirements process runs **~2 years**. Steps 1–9 repeat whenever something changes:

```
new ingest batch (feedback wave, study, sales update, competitor launch, web refresh)
  → re-extract / update findings (only affected ones)
  → derive new drafts; drafts that restate an existing requirement (any line) become `extend` proposals, not duplicates (D-035)
  → future-need projection refresh
  → prioritization run (snapshot of all requirement-target scores & ranks)
  → change proposals (priority / content / link_finding / new_requirement / extend) → PM accepts/rejects
  → history: priority timeline per requirement with the "why" of each move
```

## Evidence levels

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **E1 Strong** | Multiple independent T1 sources agree (verbatims across sources + study gap and/or sales signal) |
| **E2 Moderate** | One strong T1 source, or T1 + T2 |
| **E3 Weak** | Few verbatims or external-only (T2/T3) |
| **E4 Assumption** | Forward-looking trend/expectation without current customer evidence |

## Gates

- **Brand fit = fail** → the requirement cannot be approved without a PM override + rationale (`service.override_gate`).
- **Feasibility** = realization context only (D-030): checked and shown, never blocking, not scored.
- Fit checks: luna first, every warn/fail re-checked by sol (final verdict). `market` fit feeds a score modifier.

## Evidence level (per target, deterministic)

| Level | Rule (verbatims = distinct verbatims of the target's derivative × market behind supporting findings) |
|---|---|
| E1 | ≥ 20 verbatims from ≥ 2 channels AND (study gap supports it OR a T1/T2 web finding) |
| E2 | ≥ 15 verbatims, OR ≥ 3 verbatims + study/T1–T2 web, OR study + T1–T2 web |
| E3 | any verbatim, study item or web finding |
| E4 | nothing but assumptions |

The requirement-level `evidence_level` = best target level.

## Prioritization (scoring v1, D-029)

`score = 100 × Σ wᵢ·vᵢ / Σ wᵢ (over factors WITH data for this target) × confidence + market-fit modifier + effort modifier`, clipped 0–100.

| Factor (vᵢ ∈ 0–1) | Default weight | How |
|---|---|---|
| Customer voice | 30 | severity-weighted share of the market's in-scope feedback behind the supporting verbatim findings (log-saturating); support questions ×0.5; **no data** if the market has < 30 in-scope verbatims (CN, G70 EU) |
| Satisfaction gap | 15 | linked study items for this model × market: −z/2 (pain) or +z/2 (must-not-lose); **no data** before wave 2 / without a linked item |
| Market volume | 15 | BMW sales file (relative only, Q-015): 0.75 × units / max units + 0.25 × 2030 momentum |
| Competitive pressure | 15 | tier-weighted sources of linked competitor-advantage / review-criticism web findings for the market (4 = saturated) |
| Future relevance | 15 | horizon (today 0.3 / successor 0.6) + Kano drift to basic (+0.2) + trend/expectation findings (+0.1 each, ≤ 0.4) |
| Portfolio leverage | 10 | targets / 4 (+0.2 platform-wide) |
| Confidence | multiplier | E1 1.0 · E2 0.92 · E3 0.8 · E4 0.65 |
| Market fit | modifier | pass +2 · warn −5 · fail −10 |
| Effort | modifier | S 0 · M −3 · L −6 |

- Missing factors are renormalized and listed as **evidence gaps** on screen — a market is not punished for missing data, but its evidence level and confidence stay honest (fixes the CN bias of v3).
- Proposed priority bands: **Must ≥ 60, Should ≥ 45, Could < 45**. The AI proposal is shown next to the PM-confirmed priority.
- Every target shows its factor breakdown, gaps, modifiers and a plain-language rationale; weights are PM-editable and versioned (`weights_version`, audited).

## Continuous re-prioritization (D-013)

- Every prioritization run snapshots score, breakdown, rank and priority per requirement-target.
- Scores may be recomputed automatically (logged); **priority and status changes are only proposed** (`change_proposal`) and need a PM decision.
- Each proposal states its cause: which new evidence, weight change, or market shift moved it, and by how much per factor.
- The PM sees a priority timeline per requirement and a "what changed since last run" view.

# Requirement Model, Evidence Levels & Prioritization

**Status: v4 — as built** (scoring v1, D-029, resolves Q-004; evidence levels computed per target; feasibility non-blocking D-030). Code: `bmw_req/pipeline/scoring.py`.

## Requirement fields (all required by BMW deliverable + our additions)

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` | Global `REQ-0001`, stable forever |
| `targets` | One or more (derivative × market) with realization type: `carry_over`, `platform_wide`, `derivative_specific`, `market_variant`, `package`. **Each target has its own score, priority and fit result** (D-011) |
| `horizon` | `today` (fix/keep) or `at_successor_launch` (projected 3–5 yr need) (D-012) |
| `kano_class` / `kano_drift` | basic / performance / delighter, and expected drift by SOP (e.g. delighter → basic) |
| `title` / `description` | Customer-facing, actionable, solution-neutral where possible |
| `category` | Exterior · Interior · Comfort & Space · Infotainment & Digital · Driving Experience · Powertrain (as experienced) · Range & Charging · Driver Assistance (as experienced, scope Q-016) · Variants & Packages · Design & Quality Perception. Powertrain and Driver Assistance follow BMW's process image (image_2) |
| `target_metric` / `acceptance_criteria` | Measurable where possible |
| `linked_findings` → sources | Every requirement ≥ 1 finding; every finding ≥ 1 source |
| `fit_checks` | brand / segment / market / feasibility per target — pass / warn / fail + rationale |
| `score`, `score_breakdown`, `priority` | Per target; Must / Should / Could from score + PM decision; full history via `score_snapshot` |
| `rationale` | Plain-language explanation of score |
| `evidence_level` | See below |
| `assumptions` / `uncertainties` | Forward-looking (3–5 yr) beliefs and what could make them wrong |
| `conflicting_evidence` | Contradicting sources — shown, not hidden |
| `status` | `proposed` → `in_review` → `approved` / `rejected` / `deferred`; `challenged` loops back to `proposed`. AI may only create in `proposed` and set nothing else; every other transition is human (PM) with rationale (AGENTS rule 5) |

## Evidence levels

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **E1 Strong** | Multiple independent T1 sources agree (verbatims across sources + study gap and/or sales signal) |
| **E2 Moderate** | One strong T1 source, or T1 + T2 |
| **E3 Weak** | Few verbatims or external-only (T2/T3) |
| **E4 Assumption** | Forward-looking trend/expectation without current customer evidence |

## Gates

- **Brand fit = fail** → the requirement cannot be approved without a PM override + rationale (`service.override_gate`).
- **Feasibility** = realization context only (D-030): checked and shown, never blocking, not scored.
- Fit checks: luna first, every warn/fail re-checked by sol (final verdict). `market` fit feeds a score modifier.

## Evidence level (per target, deterministic)

| Level | Rule (verbatims = distinct verbatims of the target's derivative × market behind supporting findings) |
|---|---|
| E1 | ≥ 20 verbatims from ≥ 2 channels AND (study gap supports it OR a T1/T2 web finding) |
| E2 | ≥ 15 verbatims, OR ≥ 3 verbatims + study/T1–T2 web, OR study + T1–T2 web |
| E3 | any verbatim, study item or web finding |
| E4 | nothing but assumptions |

The requirement-level `evidence_level` = best target level.

## Prioritization (scoring v1, D-029)

`score = 100 × Σ wᵢ·vᵢ / Σ wᵢ (over factors WITH data for this target) × confidence + market-fit modifier + effort modifier`, clipped 0–100.

| Factor (vᵢ ∈ 0–1) | Default weight | How |
|---|---|---|
| Customer voice | 30 | severity-weighted share of the market's in-scope feedback behind the supporting verbatim findings (log-saturating); support questions ×0.5; **no data** if the market has < 30 in-scope verbatims (CN, G70 EU) |
| Satisfaction gap | 15 | linked study items for this model × market: −z/2 (pain) or +z/2 (must-not-lose); **no data** before wave 2 / without a linked item |
| Market volume | 15 | BMW sales file (relative only, Q-015): 0.75 × units / max units + 0.25 × 2030 momentum |
| Competitive pressure | 15 | tier-weighted sources of linked competitor-advantage / review-criticism web findings for the market (4 = saturated) |
| Future relevance | 15 | horizon (today 0.3 / successor 0.6) + Kano drift to basic (+0.2) + trend/expectation findings (+0.1 each, ≤ 0.4) |
| Portfolio leverage | 10 | targets / 4 (+0.2 platform-wide) |
| Confidence | multiplier | E1 1.0 · E2 0.92 · E3 0.8 · E4 0.65 |
| Market fit | modifier | pass +2 · warn −5 · fail −10 |
| Effort | modifier | S 0 · M −3 · L −6 |

- Missing factors are renormalized and listed as **evidence gaps** on screen — a market is not punished for missing data, but its evidence level and confidence stay honest (fixes the CN bias of v3).
- Proposed priority bands: **Must ≥ 60, Should ≥ 45, Could < 45**. The AI proposal is shown next to the PM-confirmed priority.
- Every target shows its factor breakdown, gaps, modifiers and a plain-language rationale; weights are PM-editable and versioned (`weights_version`, audited).

## Continuous re-prioritization (D-013)

- Every prioritization run snapshots score, breakdown, rank and priority per requirement-target.
- Scores may be recomputed automatically (logged); **priority and status changes are only proposed** (`change_proposal`) and need a PM decision.
- Each proposal states its cause: which new evidence, weight change, or market shift moved it, and by how much per factor.
- The PM sees a priority timeline per requirement and a "what changed since last run" view.

174	  → future-need projection refresh
175	  → prioritization run (snapshot of all requirement-target scores & ranks)
176	  → change proposals (priority / content / link_finding / new_requirement / extend) → PM accepts/rejects
177	  → history: priority timeline per requirement with the "why" of each move
178	```
179	
180	Triggers: `new_evidence`, `weight_change`, `pm_request`, `scheduled`. Evidence has a freshness decay; stale evidence loses weight unless re-confirmed.
181	
182	### Markets are distinct customer groups (D-011)
183	
184	Findings are segmented by market; every requirement-target (derivative × market) has its **own** score, priority and fit result. A `market_profile` (climate, usage, culture, infrastructure) feeds extraction, projection and fit checks. Cross-market conflicts are flagged with realization options (global / market variant / package).
185	
186	### Future needs (D-012)
187	
188	Step 5 includes **future-need projection**: predecessor findings + competitor trajectory + trends + market profile → need at successor SOP, with horizon (`today` / `at_successor_launch`) and Kano class + expected drift.
189	
190	**Mandatory human gates:** final status of every requirement; overriding a failed brand-fit or feasibility check; accepting curated reference data (platform/plant facts). Optional gates: accepting web sources, merging/splitting findings, changing weights.
191	
192	## Core data model (draft)
193	
194	### Reference layer (portfolio)
195	```
196	brand(id, name, group, positioning, core_values[], guardrails_json, source_ids[])
197	segment(id, name, e.g. premium_compact | upper_mid | luxury, description)
198	platform(id e.g. CLAR | FAAR | NK, owner_brand_group, powertrains_supported[], introduced, phase_out, successor_platform_id, source_ids[])
199	vehicle_model(id e.g. G60, brand_id, line "5 Series", body, segment_id, platform_id, generation,
200	              sop, eop_planned, powertrains[], is_bmw_group, market_variants[])   -- BMW + competitors in one table
201	market(code EU | US | CN | RoW, countries[])
202	market_profile(market_code, climate, usage_patterns, cultural_expectations, infrastructure, powertrain_mix, source_ids[], valid_from)
203	plant(id, name, city, country, platforms_supported[], powertrains_supported[], nk_ready_from, capacity_note, source_ids[])
204	production(vehicle_model_id, plant_id, market_variant e.g. "G68 LWB", markets_served[], since, until)
205	sales(vehicle_model_id, market_code, year, units, is_forecast, source_id)
206	```
207	
208	### Evidence layer
209	```
210	source_item(id, kind[feedback|study|sales|option_list|web|reference], trust_tier[T1..T3],
211	            vehicle_model_id?, market_code?, platform_id?, ref, url?, published_at?, retrieved_at,
212	            text, quote, meta_json)
213	finding(id, type, title, summary, scope_level[derivative|platform|market|portfolio],
214	        metrics_json, created_by, created_at)
215	finding_scope(finding_id, vehicle_model_id?, market_code?, platform_id?)
216	finding_source(finding_id, source_item_id, quote, relation[supports|contradicts])
217	```
218	
219	### Decision layer
220	```
221	requirement(id "REQ-0001", title, description, category, target_metric, acceptance_criteria,
222	            horizon[today|at_successor_launch], kano_class[basic|performance|delighter], kano_drift,
223	            evidence_level, assumptions, uncertainties, conflicting_evidence,
224	            status, version)                                   -- content versioned; old versions kept
225	requirement_target(requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code,
226	                   realization[carry_over|platform_wide|derivative_specific|market_variant|package],
227	                   score, score_breakdown_json, priority, rationale)   -- per-market priority (D-011)
228	requirement_finding(requirement_id, finding_id, relation[supports|contradicts])
229	fit_check(id, requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code, check[brand|segment|market|feasibility],
230	          result[pass|warn|fail], rationale, evidence_source_ids[], checked_by, checked_at)
231	audit_event(id, ts, actor_type[ai|human|system], actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id,
232	            field, old_value, new_value, rationale, model, prompt_ref)   -- append-only
233	```
234	
235	### Continuity layer (D-013)
236	```
237	ingest_batch(id, ts, kind[feedback_wave|study|sales|competitor_event|web_refresh], description, source_ids[])
238	prioritization_run(id, ts, trigger[new_evidence|weight_change|pm_request|scheduled], ingest_batch_id?,
239	                   weights_version, model, initiated_by)
240	score_snapshot(run_id, requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code, score, breakdown_json, rank, priority)
241	change_proposal(id, run_id, requirement_id, target?, kind[priority|content|link_finding|new_requirement|extend], field,
242	                old_value, proposed_value, reason, evidence_delta_json, status[open|accepted|rejected|superseded], decided_by, decided_at, decision_rationale)
243	weights_version(id, weights_json, created_by, created_at, rationale)
244	llm_usage(id, ts, job, model, status, reserved_usd, cost_usd, tokens…, search_calls)   -- budget guard (D-014)
245	llm_cache(key, model, output_text, llm_usage_id)   -- identical requests never re-billed (D-010)
246	```
247	
248	Requirement IDs are global (`REQ-0001`); scope lives in `requirement_target`, so one requirement can apply to several derivatives/markets (e.g. an infotainment UX fix across all CLAR cars).
249	
250	## Audit trail rules
251	
252	- Append-only: no UPDATE/DELETE on `audit_event` (enforced by SQLite triggers).
253	- Every mutation of requirement content, targets, score, priority, evidence links, fit checks or status → one event (who/what, when, before/after, rationale).
254	- AI events record model name + prompt/agent version; web research events record queries and URLs.
255	- Access events (view/export) logged as well.
256	
257	## Key UI views (planned)
258	
259	- **Organised by the PM's job (D-036):** *Start here* = Home (question, wave stepper, what needs a decision, top priorities), Review requirements (guided queue, one requirement at a time in plain language), Priorities by market (Must/Should/Could board + market comparison), AI suggestions (the change inbox), plus How it works (D-037: one requirement traced step by step — rule for all data on the left, its concrete effect on this requirement on the right, score as a waterfall). *Explore & trace* and *Under the hood* hold the detail views below. Optional demo tour (8 steps).
260	- **Portfolio matrix** — derivatives × markets, with platform and plant, sales trend, top findings, requirement count.
261	- **Requirement detail** — evidence chain (sources → findings → requirement), fit checks, score breakdown, audit timeline, approve/reject/edit/challenge.
262	- **Competitor view** — per segment × market: who sells what, strengths, gaps vs. BMW.
263	- **Ranked backlog** — per market (EU / US / CN side by side), adjustable weights, visible re-ranking diff.
264	- **Priority history** — timeline per requirement across prioritization runs, each move annotated with its cause (new evidence, weight change, PM decision).
265	- **Change inbox** — open AI change proposals after a new ingest batch; PM accepts/rejects with rationale.
266	- **Market conflict view** — requirements whose priority diverges strongly between markets, with realization options.
267	# Requirement Model, Evidence Levels & Prioritization
268	
269	**Status: v4 — as built** (scoring v1, D-029, resolves Q-004; evidence levels computed per target; feasibility non-blocking D-030). Code: `bmw_req/pipeline/scoring.py`.
270	
271	## Requirement fields (all required by BMW deliverable + our additions)
272	
273	| Field | Notes |
274	|---|---|
275	| `id` | Global `REQ-0001`, stable forever |
276	| `targets` | One or more (derivative × market) with realization type: `carry_over`, `platform_wide`, `derivative_specific`, `market_variant`, `package`. **Each target has its own score, priority and fit result** (D-011) |
277	| `horizon` | `today` (fix/keep) or `at_successor_launch` (projected 3–5 yr need) (D-012) |
278	| `kano_class` / `kano_drift` | basic / performance / delighter, and expected drift by SOP (e.g. delighter → basic) |
279	| `title` / `description` | Customer-facing, actionable, solution-neutral where possible |
280	| `category` | Exterior · Interior · Comfort & Space · Infotainment & Digital · Driving Experience · Powertrain (as experienced) · Range & Charging · Driver Assistance (as experienced, scope Q-016) · Variants & Packages · Design & Quality Perception. Powertrain and Driver Assistance follow BMW's process image (image_2) |
281	| `target_metric` / `acceptance_criteria` | Measurable where possible |
282	| `linked_findings` → sources | Every requirement ≥ 1 finding; every finding ≥ 1 source |
283	| `fit_checks` | brand / segment / market / feasibility per target — pass / warn / fail + rationale |
284	| `score`, `score_breakdown`, `priority` | Per target; Must / Should / Could from score + PM decision; full history via `score_snapshot` |
285	| `rationale` | Plain-language explanation of score |
286	| `evidence_level` | See below |
287	| `assumptions` / `uncertainties` | Forward-looking (3–5 yr) beliefs and what could make them wrong |
288	| `conflicting_evidence` | Contradicting sources — shown, not hidden |
289	| `status` | `proposed` → `in_review` → `approved` / `rejected` / `deferred`; `challenged` loops back to `proposed`. AI may only create in `proposed` and set nothing else; every other transition is human (PM) with rationale (AGENTS rule 5) |
290	
291	## Evidence levels
292	
293	| Level | Meaning |
294	|---|---|
295	| **E1 Strong** | Multiple independent T1 sources agree (verbatims across sources + study gap and/or sales signal) |
296	| **E2 Moderate** | One strong T1 source, or T1 + T2 |
297	| **E3 Weak** | Few verbatims or external-only (T2/T3) |
298	| **E4 Assumption** | Forward-looking trend/expectation without current customer evidence |
299	
300	## Gates
301	
302	- **Brand fit = fail** → the requirement cannot be approved without a PM override + rationale (`service.override_gate`).
303	- **Feasibility** = realization context only (D-030): checked and shown, never blocking, not scored.
304	- Fit checks: luna first, every warn/fail re-checked by sol (final verdict). `market` fit feeds a score modifier.
305	
306	## Evidence level (per target, deterministic)
307	
308	| Level | Rule (verbatims = distinct verbatims of the target's derivative × market behind supporting findings) |
309	|---|---|
310	| E1 | ≥ 20 verbatims from ≥ 2 channels AND (study gap supports it OR a T1/T2 web finding) |
311	| E2 | ≥ 15 verbatims, OR ≥ 3 verbatims + study/T1–T2 web, OR study + T1–T2 web |
312	| E3 | any verbatim, study item or web finding |
313	| E4 | nothing but assumptions |
314	
315	The requirement-level `evidence_level` = best target level.
316	
317	## Prioritization (scoring v1, D-029)
318	
319	`score = 100 × Σ wᵢ·vᵢ / Σ wᵢ (over factors WITH data for this target) × confidence + market-fit modifier + effort modifier`, clipped 0–100.
320	
321	| Factor (vᵢ ∈ 0–1) | Default weight | How |
322	|---|---|---|
323	| Customer voice | 30 | severity-weighted share of the market's in-scope feedback behind the supporting verbatim findings (log-saturating); support questions ×0.5; **no data** if the market has < 30 in-scope verbatims (CN, G70 EU) |
324	| Satisfaction gap | 15 | linked study items for this model × market: −z/2 (pain) or +z/2 (must-not-lose); **no data** before wave 2 / without a linked item |
325	| Market volume | 15 | BMW sales file (relative only, Q-015): 0.75 × units / max units + 0.25 × 2030 momentum |
326	| Competitive pressure | 15 | tier-weighted sources of linked competitor-advantage / review-criticism web findings for the market (4 = saturated) |
327	| Future relevance | 15 | horizon (today 0.3 / successor 0.6) + Kano drift to basic (+0.2) + trend/expectation findings (+0.1 each, ≤ 0.4) |
328	| Portfolio leverage | 10 | targets / 4 (+0.2 platform-wide) |
329	| Confidence | multiplier | E1 1.0 · E2 0.92 · E3 0.8 · E4 0.65 |
330	| Market fit | modifier | pass +2 · warn −5 · fail −10 |
331	| Effort | modifier | S 0 · M −3 · L −6 |
332	
333	- Missing factors are renormalized and listed as **evidence gaps** on screen — a market is not punished for missing data, but its evidence level and confidence stay honest (fixes the CN bias of v3).
334	- Proposed priority bands: **Must ≥ 60, Should ≥ 45, Could < 45**. The AI proposal is shown next to the PM-confirmed priority.
335	- Every target shows its factor breakdown, gaps, modifiers and a plain-language rationale; weights are PM-editable and versioned (`weights_version`, audited).
336	
337	## Continuous re-prioritization (D-013)
338	
339	- Every prioritization run snapshots score, breakdown, rank and priority per requirement-target.
340	- Scores may be recomputed automatically (logged); **priority and status changes are only proposed** (`change_proposal`) and need a PM decision.
341	- Each proposal states its cause: which new evidence, weight change, or market shift moved it, and by how much per factor.
342	- The PM sees a priority timeline per requirement and a "what changed since last run" view.
343	# Knowledge Base & Web Enrichment
344	
345	**Status: DRAFT (D-007).** BMW's own customer data is not enough. The knowledge base combines internal data, curated reference data and web evidence.
346	
347	## Three layers
348	
349	| Layer | Contents | How it gets in | Changes |
350	|---|---|---|---|
351	| **1. BMW internal** | Verbatims, customer studies, sales volumes, option lists (`data-inventory.md`) | Deterministic loaders | Read-only |
352	| **2. Curated reference** | Platforms, plants (location, platforms, powertrains, NK readiness), production allocation, brand positioning + guardrails, segments, competitor model catalog | Research agents propose → human accepts | Versioned; every fact has source + date |
353	| **3. Web evidence** | Competitor features & sales, market demand & powertrain trends, professional reviews, customer expectation studies, owner forums/social | Research agents, on demand or scheduled | Append-only, timestamped |
354	
355	Seed docs: `portfolio-reference.md` (platforms, plants, BMW sales), `competitor-landscape.md` (competitors, trends, brand positioning), `bmw-annual-report-2025.md` (T1: BMW Group Report 2025 — market & sales data, R&D, NEUE KLASSE strategy, with page numbers; recommended by BMW support).
356	
357	## Research agents (OpenAI web search; orchestration via LangGraph — D-015)
358	
359	| Agent | Question it answers | Typical sources |
360	|---|---|---|
361	| **Competitor scout** | Who competes per segment × market, what they offer that BMW doesn't | OEM sites, press releases, reviews |
362	| **Market & sales analyst** | Volumes and growth by brand/model/powertrain/market; which models are in demand | ACEA, KBA, CPCA, Cox/Automotive News, OEM reports |
363	| **Review miner** | What professional reviewers and owners praise/criticize (BMW + competitors) | Car and Driver, Autocar, Auto Bild, Autohome/Dongchedi, forums |
364	| **Market profile scout** (D-011, Q-013) | Climate, real usage, culture, infrastructure and powertrain mix per market | Mobility/usage studies, climate data, J.D. Power CN/US, charging statistics |
365	| **Trend & expectation scout** | Customer expectations 3–5 years ahead (software, ADAS, charging, interior, personalization) | J.D. Power, McKinsey, Deloitte, S&P |
366	| **Brand-fit checker** | Does a requirement fit BMW brand + the derivative's segment? | Brand reference (layer 2) |
367	| **Feasibility checker** | Can the target platform/plant build it for that market at the planned time? | Platform/plant reference (layer 2) |
368	
369	Each agent returns **schema-validated structured output** (Pydantic → Responses API structured output, D-020): claim, quote, URL, publisher, published date, retrieved date, market, model(s), trust tier. Free-text LLM opinions are **never** stored as sources.
370	
371	## Trust tiers
372	
373	| Tier | Examples | Default weight |
374	|---|---|---|
375	| **T1** | BMW internal data; official OEM press/annual reports; registration statistics (KBA, ACEA, CPCA) | 1.0 |
376	| **T2** | Reputable press & analysts (Reuters, Bloomberg, Automotive News, J.D. Power, McKinsey), professional reviews | 0.8 |
377	| **T3** | Forums, social media, blogs, aggregators | 0.5 |
378	
379	Rules: prefer recent sources (flag > 24 months old); when sources disagree, store both and raise `conflicting_evidence`; facts the user supplied are stored as `T3/user-claim` until verified.
380	
381	## Brand & segment fit (D-008)
382	
383	Every requirement is checked against the brand profile (BMW: driving pleasure, sportiness, driver focus, premium quality, design, innovation) and the derivative's segment. Example: a "budget, efficiency-first family hatch" spec contradicts BMW positioning → `fail`, regardless of how loudly a generic market trend demands it. Guardrails live in `brand.guardrails_json`, seeded from `competitor-landscape.md`.
384	
385	## Platform & plant feasibility (D-009)
386	
387	For each `requirement_target`: is the derivative's platform (and its successor, e.g. NK) able to carry the requirement; does a plant that builds this platform + powertrain serve that market; is the timing compatible with NK rollout? Output `pass / warn / fail` + rationale. This is a **feasibility filter on customer requirements**, not an engineering spec (scope stays customer-facing).
388

"""Requirement derivation from extracted signals (sol). Pilot version."""

import json
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from bmw_req.llm import LLM
from bmw_req.pipeline.extract import Category


class RequirementDraft(BaseModel):
    title: str
    description: str = Field(description="Customer-facing, solution-neutral where possible")
    category: Category
    target_metric: str
    acceptance_criteria: str
    horizon: Literal["today", "at_successor_launch"]
    horizon_reason: str
    kano_class: Literal["basic", "performance", "delighter"]
    kano_drift: str = Field(description="Expected Kano class at successor launch and why, or 'stable'")
    evidence_verbatim_ids: list[str] = Field(description="IDs of the verbatims that support this requirement")
    conflicting_verbatim_ids: list[str]
    assumptions: str
    uncertainties: str


class DerivationResult(BaseModel):
    requirements: list[RequirementDraft]


INSTRUCTIONS = """You are a product requirements analyst for the successor of a BMW vehicle (launch in 3-5 years).
Input: customer signals extracted from verbatims (with verbatim IDs), for one derivative and market.
Derive exactly {n} customer requirements, the most important ones the evidence supports.
Rules:
- Every requirement must cite the verbatim IDs that support it; use only IDs from the input. Cite contradicting ones too.
- Customer-facing requirements only: no engineering/component specs, no pricing, no regulatory items.
- Must fit a premium BMW in this segment.
- Separate evidence from assumption: put forward-looking beliefs in `assumptions`, and what could make them wrong in `uncertainties`.
- target_metric / acceptance_criteria: measurable from the customer's point of view, with a concrete proposed
  target value (e.g. "≥ 95 % automatic reconnects"). Mark every target value as a proposal in `assumptions`.
- horizon: `today` = a current shortcoming to fix or strength to keep, needed regardless of trends.
  `at_successor_launch` = only when you expect the need itself to grow or change by launch in 3-5 years;
  say why in horizon_reason. Do not default to either one.
- kano_class: `basic` = customers take it for granted and are dissatisfied only by its absence or failure
  (reliability, things that must simply work); `performance` = more is better, satisfaction scales with it
  (range, comfort, speed of response); `delighter` = unexpected, absence goes unnoticed. Classify by how
  customers react today; put the expected change by launch in kano_drift.
- Do not invent customer statements; the evidence base is small, say so in uncertainties where relevant."""


def derive(llm: LLM, context: dict, signals: list[dict], *, n: int, job: str, demo: bool = False):
    res = llm.generate(
        job=job,
        tier="smart",
        instructions=INSTRUCTIONS.format(n=n),
        input=json.dumps({"context": context, "signals": signals}, ensure_ascii=False),
        schema=DerivationResult,
        reasoning_effort="medium",
        max_output_tokens=16_000,

# Plan v2 — beyond customer comments (2026-10-11)

Owner: agent session `ehl-munich-final-e3`, branch `feat/v2-multi-trigger` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/v2`, own DB copy).
Asked by Atahan, 2026-10-11. Inputs:
- BMW support's message on the annual report: market & sales data, product strategy & R&D.
- Atahan's review:
  - Customer feedback is the only real trigger.
  - Compliance and regulation are missing.
  - Public reviews across brands are missing.
  - There's no explanation of why Chinese brands are winning.
  - Customers aren't grouped.
  - Models aren't grouped.
  - There's no offering per market.

Decision numbers for this work: **D-040+**, questions **Q-026+** (the 3D-view session holds D-039 / Q-025).

## 1. Diagnosis (what the current system skips)

| BMW process box (image_2) | Today | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline: previous model | Verbatims + study on the predecessor | Option list (458 items) is ingested but never used to decide anything |
| Baseline: BMW portfolio | Platforms, plants (feasibility only) | No "what other BMW models / NK already have" as a trigger (carry-over, NK flow-down) |
| Baseline: sales volume | Market volume factor (stylized file) | Annual report T1 facts (regional growth, EV share, model-series trends) not in the DB |
| Competition | 47 competitor_advantage web findings, used only as scoring support | Competitors never *originate* a requirement |
| Customer / public feedback | BMW verbatims only | No public owner reviews, no cross-brand view |
| Product & global trends | 20 trend + 26 expectation findings | Trends never originate; 31/39 requirements are `today` |
| Structure: "all potential requirements (0/1)" | Requirements exist only if derived from clusters | No candidate catalogue with an explicit implement yes/no per derivative × market |
| Requirements definition: groups | Categories exist | Powertrain / Driver assistance thin (5 each) |
| Prioritization: Customer / Business / … | One blended score | No visible Customer vs Business split; no strategic alignment; no compliance dimension |

## 2. Pillars

Each pillar gets its own decision entry when built.

**P1 — Multi-trigger requirements (image_2 "Situation analysis").**
- Every requirement gets an `origin` (trigger lane): customer voice, competitor gap, trend / future need, BMW baseline & portfolio (predecessor option list, NK / OS X flow-down), strategy (annual report), regulation-driven.
- A **candidate catalogue** (the "0/1 list") is built from:
  - option lists;
  - a competitor feature matrix;
  - trends;
  - regulation.
- Each candidate gets an implement yes/no proposal per derivative × market, with its evidence. Candidates with a yes become requirements through the same derivation, linker, fit and scoring steps.
- The evidence mix per requirement is shown, e.g. "60 % customer voice, 25 % competitors, 15 % trends".

**P2 — Regulatory & compliance radar** (scope reconciliation, decision needed: D-040).
- BMW's brief puts regulatory *requirements* out of scope. Atahan wants compliance in. Reconciliation: regulation is **context, trigger and gate**, never an output spec.
  - (a) A `regulation` reference table: EU / US / CN, title, status, effective date, T1 source, customer-facing consequence. Examples to verify:
    - Euro NCAP 2026 physical controls;
    - China's 2027 door-handle rule;
    - China's L2 ADAS marketing / OTA rules;
    - EU GSR2 ISA / driver monitoring;
    - UN R155 / R156 OTA;
    - EU Data Act;
    - China data export rules.
  - (b) A `compliance` fit check per target: `pass` (no conflict) / `warn` (affected, needs adaptation) / `fail` (conflicts with binding regulation in that market).
  - (c) Regulation-triggered *customer-facing* requirements, e.g. "the most-used functions are reachable without touchscreen menus", not "comply with ECE R…".
  - (d) A Regulatory radar page.

**P3 — Customer groups and model groups.**
- Personas, for example:
  - driving purist / enthusiast;
  - digital-first;
  - comfort & chauffeur (China LWB rear seat);
  - family & practical;
  - status & design;
  - pragmatic EV switcher.
- Personas are evidence-backed: signal-level persona tags (cheap model), web / annual-report sources, and the persona mix per derivative × market.
- Model groups by segment, body, powertrain and platform (CLAR / FAAR → NK).
- Requirements carry the personas they serve. Priorities can be viewed per persona. Must-not-lose traits per persona (e.g. the enthusiast's steering feel) protect against "one average customer".

**P4 — Market offering strategy (variants & packages, in scope).**
- For configurable items (option-list items + catalogue candidates), propose per derivative × market one of: standard, package, optional, or don't offer.
- Factors:
  - rough price (option list, as effort proxy only — no business case);
  - market saturation (share of competitors with it as standard);
  - customer expectation (study, verbatims, persona mix);
  - competitive pressure.
- Shown as an offering matrix with a rationale per cell. Each row is a proposal for the PM.

**P5 — Public reviews and market intelligence.**
- Find aggregators of owner reviews and ratings across brands, for example:
  - NHTSA complaints API (US, official);
  - J.D. Power APEAL / IQS / China studies;
  - Autohome / Dongchedi owner ratings (CN);
  - Edmunds / Cars.com;
  - What Car?.
- Ingest only what's allowed and cite it.
- Combine with registration and sales data (CPCA, KBA / ACEA, US) for a **"why" analysis** per market:
  - why Chinese brands grow;
  - how BMW regains China share;
  - where BMW can grow in Europe;
  - US powertrain shift.
- Output: cited market-strategy findings (T1–T3) that feed the competitor and strategy lanes. Correlation is labelled as correlation, never as cause.

**P6 — Annual report as T1 evidence (BMW support's message).**
- Annual report facts become `source_item(kind=reference, T1)` with page numbers:
  - regional growth, model-series deliveries, EV share by region;

input.prompt:
You are a research agent for a BMW hackathon app (AI that derives prioritized *customer-facing* requirements for successor BMW vehicles: 1 Series F70, 5 Series G60 / China LWB G68, 7 Series G70; markets EU, US, CN, plus RoW = Japan/Korea; successor launches ~2028–2031).

Do NOT edit code, the DB, or any existing file. Do NOT read anything in `challange information document/` (confidential, not needed). Do not send any BMW-internal data to web searches.

TASK — "Regulatory & compliance radar". BMW's brief says regulatory/homologation requirements are OUT of scope as outputs, so we use regulation as context, trigger and gate: which binding or upcoming regulations (and quasi-regulatory rating programs like Euro NCAP, C-NCAP, IIHS) change what customers experience in the car, per market, between 2025 and ~2032. Use WebSearch/WebFetch. Prefer T1 sources (official regulator/legal text: EUR-Lex, UNECE, MIIT/SAMR/CAC, NHTSA/Federal Register, Euro NCAP protocols), then T2 (Reuters, Automotive News, law-firm briefings). Verify every claim; record URL, publisher, publish date, retrieved date 2026-10-11, and a short exact quote.

Candidates to verify (and find others): Euro NCAP 2026 protocol rewarding physical controls (indicators, hazards, horn, wipers, eCall); China MIIT mandatory standard on door handles (mechanical release, flush handles) from 2027; China MIIT rules after the 2025 Xiaomi SU7 crash on L2 ADAS marketing terms ("autonomous", "smart driving"), OTA updates needing approval, beta testing ban; China L2 ADAS mandatory national standard; China data security / car data export rules (CAC); EU GSR2 (ISA speed limit warning, driver drowsiness/attention, DDAW/ADDW, EDR) and customer annoyance with ISA beeps; UN R155/R156 cybersecurity/software updates (consequence: OTA, feature unavailability e.g. in older cars); UN R157/R171 (DCAS) hands-off driving in EU; EU Data Act (Sept 2025) customer access to vehicle data; EU battery regulation (battery passport, state of health); Euro 7 (brake dust, battery durability — customer-facing consequence: battery health guarantee); EU AFIR (charging payment by card, price transparency); EU CO2 fleet targets 2025–2035 and the 2035 combustion phase-out debate (consequence: powertrain availability per market); US: NHTSA AEB rule FMVSS 127 (2029), US EV tax credit end (Sept 2025), US tariffs; US ban on Chinese connected-vehicle software/hardware (BIS rule, MY2027/2030) — consequence for infotainment partners; China NEV purchase tax changes 2026–2027; China mandatory requirements on screen/HMI distraction if any; EU right-to-repair; accessibility; seat/child-seat ISOFIX/i-Size; Japan/Korea where relevant. Also mirror-cameras, light signatures (illuminated grilles regulations), sound (AVAS), subscription/feature-on-demand consumer-protection rulings.

For each regulation produce: id (REG-XX-nn), jurisdiction (EU/US/CN/UNECE/JP/KR/global), title, instrument type (law / mandatory standard / rating program / guidance), status (in force / adopted / proposed / debated), key dates (adopted, applies to new types, applies to all new registrations), affected categories from this list [Exterior, Interior, Comfort & Space, Infotainment & Digital, Driving Experience, Powertrain (as experienced), Range & Charging, Driver Assistance (as experienced), Variants & Packages, Design & Quality Perception], customer-facing consequence (one plain sentence: what changes for the driver), opportunity (how a customer-facing requirement can turn this into value), risk/conflict (which kind of feature would conflict — e.g. hidden flush door handles, touch-only hazard switch, "autopilot" naming), affected models (F70/G60/G68/G70 + markets), trust tier, sources [{url, publisher, published, retrieved, quote}].

OUTPUTS (exactly these two files):
1. `data/seed/regulations.json` — a JSON array of the objects above (valid JSON; keys snake_case).
2. `foundation/documents/regulatory-radar.md` — concise human doc: purpose + scope line (regulation as context/trigger/gate, never an output spec — BMW brief), a table per market, then "Top 8 customer-facing implications for successor BMWs" with citations, then "Unverified / conflicting" section. Plain, clear English, short sentences.

Quality bar: only include items you verified from a source you actually opened; mark uncertain items status "unverified" rather than inventing. Aim for 20–35 regulations. Final message to me: counts per jurisdiction, the 8 implications in one line each, and anything surprising.
